tasks.label: General Site / Workshop
tasks.note: Baseline for everyone entering the work area.

tasks.label: Welding and Cutting
tasks.note: Arc, sparks and fumes: protect eyes, skin, lungs.

tasks.label: Grinding / Machining
tasks.note: Flying particles and noise; avoid loose gloves near rotating parts.

tasks.label: Electrical Work
tasks.note: Arc rated PPE and insulated tools; follow energy study.

tasks.label: High-Noise Area
tasks.note: Above 85 dB(A) means protection is required.

tasks.label: Painting / Spraying
tasks.note: Vapours and mists; ventilation and respirators.

hard_hat.name: Safety Helmet
hard_hat.protects_against: Falling objects, bumps, overhead strikes and some electrical contact
choose: Choose Class E (electrical) when near live parts.
Use Type II where side impact is possible.
Fit a chin strap for work at height or in wind.
Check the date stamp; replace at manufacturer's age limit.

safety_glasses.name: Safety Glasses
choose: Choose side shields for grinding and machining.
Use anti-fog, scratch-resistant lenses.
Wear over prescription glasses only if designed for it, or use prescription safety glasses.

goggles.name: Safety Goggles
goggles.protects_against: Chemical splash, fine dust, molten metal splash
choose: Use indirect-vent goggles for liquids and sealed goggles for fine dust or gas.
Check the strap is elastic and seals against the face.
Never use direct-vent goggles for chemical splash.

face_shield.name: Face Shield
choose: Always wear safety glasses underneath.
Choose polycarbonate for impact and acetate for chemical splash.
Pick an arc-rated shield for electrical arc risk.

hearing.name: Hearing Protection
choose: Pick enough attenuation to bring exposure below 85 dB(A) at the ear without overprotecting.
Earmuffs for intermittent noise; plugs for long wear or hot places.
Use both plugs and muffs above about 105 dB(A).
Train workers on correct insertion.

respirator.name: Respirator / Dust Mask
choose: Match the filter to the contaminant: particulate (P), organic vapour (A), acid gas (B/E), combined.
Fit-test every tight-fitting respirator; no facial hair on the seal.
Use supplied-air or SCBA in oxygen-deficient or IDLH atmospheres.
Replace filters by schedule or when breathing resistance or smell appears.

gloves_cut.name: Cut / Mechanical Gloves

standards.canada: No single CSA code; use ANSI/ISEA 105 or EN 388 ratings

choose: Pick the cut level for the blade or sheet edge risk.
Do NOT wear gloves near rotating machinery where entanglement is a risk.
Choose grip coating suited to oily or dry work.

gloves_chem.name: Chemical-Resistant Gloves
choose: Select the glove material for the specific chemical using the manufacturer's breakthrough chart (nitrile, neoprene, butyl, PVC, Viton).
Check glove thickness and length.
Never reuse disposable gloves; change before breakthrough time.

gloves_heat.name: Heat / Welding Gloves
gloves_heat.protects_against: Hot surfaces, sparks, molten splash, radiant heat
choose: Match contact heat level and flame rating to the job.
Use long gauntlet cuffs for welding.
Keep dry; wet gloves transmit heat quickly.

safety_shoes.name: Safety Footwear
safety_shoes.protects_against: Crush, puncture, slips, electrical and chemical hazards
choose: Toe cap (steel or composite) and puncture-resistant midsole for sites with nails.
Anti-slip sole for wet or oily floors.
Metatarsal guards for heavy handling.
Use EH-rated for electrical hazard and ESD for electronics.

hi_vis.name: High-Visibility Clothing
hi_vis.protects_against: Being struck by vehicles or machinery
choose: Choose the class by traffic speed and visibility.
Fluorescent yellow/orange for day; add retroreflective strips for night.
Replace when faded or dirty.

harness.name: Full-Body Harness and Lanyard
choose: Use a full-body harness with shock-absorbing lanyard for fall arrest.
Anchor point must be rated for 15 kN (EU) or 22 kN (US) per person.
Check clearance below to avoid hitting the ground.
Have a rescue plan before work starts.

fr_clothing.name: Flame-Resistant / Arc-Rated Clothing
fr_clothing.protects_against: Flash fire, arc flash, molten metal splash
choose: Choose the arc rating (cal/cm²) from the incident energy study.
No synthetic underlayers that melt.
Do not wash with fabric softener; follow care labels.

welding_helmet.name: Welding Helmet / Shield
choose: Select shade number for the process and current (typically 10 to 14).
Auto-darkening lens should be tested before use.
Wear safety glasses underneath.

coverall.name: Coverall / Work Clothing
choose: Choose close-fitting, no loose cuffs or dangling parts near machines.
Natural fibre or FR fabric for hot work.
Washable and replaceable as per condition.

selection_rules: PPE is the last line of defence: first try to eliminate, substitute, isolate or guard (hierarchy of controls).
Choose PPE based on a documented hazard assessment for the specific task, not on habit.
Pick certified PPE that bears the correct standard mark and is suitable for the workplace.
Make sure the PPE fits the individual; ill-fitting PPE offers less protection and is not worn.
Combine items so they work together (e.g. glasses under a face shield, hearing protection under a helmet).
Train workers on when to use, how to wear, limits, care and disposal.
Never mix up PPE: protection from one hazard can create another (loose gloves near rotating parts).
Provide it free to workers and replace it when worn, damaged or past its service life.
verifyNote: Standards listed are commonly applied references and are updated from time to time. Always verify the current edition and local legal requirements with your regulator, supplier or competent safety professional before purchase or use.

inspection.name: Safety Helmet
before_use: Check shell for cracks, dents, chalking or discolouration.
Check harness, suspension and chin strap for wear.
Read the date stamp inside the shell.
reject_if: Any crack, deep gouge or impact history.
care: Clean with mild soap and water.
Store away from sunlight, heat and solvents.
Do not drill holes or paint with solvent paint.
inspection.life: Typically 3 to 5 years (supplier dependent); replace immediately after a heavy impact.

inspection.name: Eye and Face Protection
before_use: Look for scratches, haze or cracks.
Check frames and straps for damage.
Make sure lenses are clean.
reject_if: Deep scratches or pitting that affect vision.
care: Clean with lens cleaner and soft cloth.
inspection.life: Replace when scratched or damaged; no fixed life.

inspection.name: Hearing Protection
before_use: Check earmuff cups and cushions for cracks.
Check plugs are clean and flexible.
reject_if: Hardened or cracked foam or cushions.
Broken headband or loss of spring tension.
care: Replace disposable plugs after one use.
inspection.life: Disposable: single use; muff cushions about 6 to 12 months.

inspection.name: Respirator
before_use: Check straps, valves and seals.
Check filter expiry and condition.
Perform a seal check each time you wear it.
reject_if: Expired filters or higher breathing resistance.
care: Store in sealed bag away from dust and chemicals.
inspection.life: Disposable per shift or when damaged; cartridges by change schedule.

inspection.name: Gloves
before_use: Check for holes, tears, cuts and thin spots.
For chemical gloves, inflate or look for leaks.
reject_if: Stiffening, swelling, discolouration or chemical smell.
care: Wash or air dry per label.
inspection.life: Per condition; disposable gloves are single use.

inspection.name: Safety Footwear
before_use: Check soles for wear, cuts and cracks.
Check the toe cap is not exposed or dented.
Check laces and fasteners.
reject_if: Exposed toe cap or soles worn smooth.
inspection.life: Typically 6 to 12 months of heavy use; replace after impact.

inspection.name: Harness and Lanyard
before_use: Check webbing for cuts, burns, fraying or chemical damage.
Check buckles, D-rings and stitching.
Check shock absorber pack is not deployed.
reject_if: Missing inspection tag or overdue inspection.
care: Wash with mild soap; no bleach.
inspection.life: Manufacturer limit (often up to 10 years); formal inspection at least every 6 to 12 months.

inspection.name: High-Visibility Clothing
before_use: Check fluorescent colour is bright.
Check reflective tape is intact.
care: Wash at low temperature without softener.
inspection.life: Typically 25 to 50 washes or when faded.

heat_stress.principle: Heavy PPE reduces the body's ability to cool, so the PPE selection and work plan must be adjusted for hot conditions to prevent heat illness.

adjustments.issue: Impermeable chemical suits trap sweat and heat
adjustments.adjust: Limit continuous wear, use cooling vests or ventilated suits, and add rest breaks.

adjustments.issue: Heavy FR clothing in hot weather
adjustments.adjust: Use lightweight FR fabrics and plan hot work for cooler hours.
Use powered air-purifying respirators for long jobs and rotate staff.
Use ventilated helmets, cooling liners and shade breaks.

rules: Provide cool drinking water and encourage frequent small drinks; do not wait for thirst.
Acclimatise new or returning workers gradually over 1 to 2 weeks.
Use a work and rest schedule based on the WBGT heat index.
Provide shaded or cool rest areas near the work.
Watch for heat illness signs: heavy sweating, dizziness, headache, nausea, confusion, hot dry skin.
Stop work and call emergency services if someone has confusion or collapses (possible heat stroke); cool the person immediately.
Pair workers so they can monitor each other.
